name: Calendar Backspread (Back Ratio Time Spread)
summary: Sell one near-term option and buy two longer-dated options at the same strike; a defined-risk, long-vega, long-convexity time spread that pays on a big back-month move or a vol expansion.
max_profit: Unbounded in the direction of the extra long leg after front expiry (two long calls with no cap), plus the calendar payoff at the strike. Effectively two payoff regimes: pin-at-strike (calendar payoff) and big-move (backspread payoff).
max_loss: The net debit paid. Realized when spot sits between the pin zone and the convexity zone at back expiry with vol unchanged - the classic 'slow drift' loss.
breakevens: Complex two-regime profile; solve numerically. The upside breakeven after front expiry is roughly strike + (remaining debit)/200 per unit because two long calls share the cost.

greeks.delta: positive for the call version (two longs vs one short), roughly +0.20 to +0.40 per unit
greeks.gamma: positive overall once the front short is gone; slightly negative before
greeks.theta: negative to flat - you are paying for convexity
greeks.vega: strongly positive - two back-month longs; best entered at very low IV rank

when_to_use: IV rank < 20 with an expectation of a vol expansion or a large directional move over the next 2-4 months. Pairs well with a low-vol, coiled chart (Bollinger band squeeze, ATR at a 6-month low). Explicitly LEVEL 3 LEGAL: the single short front leg is covered by the first back-month long, and the second long adds no short risk.
entry_rules: IV rank < 20 AND back-month IV below its own 12-month 30th percentile.
Ratio exactly 1 short : 2 long. Never sell more fronts than there are back-month longs.
Same strike on all legs; short front |delta| 0.35-0.50.
Front 21-35 DTE, back 60-120 DTE; the back leg must be at least 45 days beyond the front.
Net debit <= 2% of equity per unit.
Realized-vol filter: 20-day realized volatility below the 25th percentile of its own 1-year range (a coiled underlying).

LEVEL 3 OK - the short front is fully covered by one of the back-month longs at the same strike and a later expiry. Submit as a 3-contract mleg; if it is rejected, buy the two back-month longs FIRST, then sell the front.
management_rules: Profit target +50% of debit (this structure is asymmetric - let winners run further than a plain calendar).
Stop at -50% of debit, or at -35% if the back-month IV has fallen 5 vol points below entry.
Roll the short front out one expiry at front DTE <= 7 for a credit, to keep financing the longs; roll at most 3 times.
If the structure becomes a pure long 2-lot after the front expires, apply plain long-call rules: stop at -50% of the remaining value, take profit at +100%.
exit_rules: Close or roll the short front leg by 14:30 ET on its expiration day, unconditionally.
Close the short immediately if extrinsic <= $0.05 or |delta| >= 0.90.
Close the short call before ex-dividend if extrinsic < dividend per share.
After the short is gone, close the remaining long pair no later than 21 DTE on the back month, or when the long premium decays below 40% of the original debit.
Buy back the short before selling any long.
assignment_risk: One short front leg, covered twice over by the back-month longs. Assignment leaves the account short 100 shares against two long calls - a covered and directionally hedged position, but it must still be flattened within one session.
buying_power: Net debit only. The extra long adds cost, not margin.
liquidity_needs: Back month 60-120 DTE must be genuinely quoted: OI >= 200, spread <= $0.20. Long-dated single-stock options are often too wide - prefer large caps and major ETFs.
common_mistakes: Entering at high IV rank and watching the two long vegas bleed; over-rolling the short and turning a convexity trade into a grind; forgetting that this structure loses on a slow drift, which is the most common market outcome.
zero_dte_notes: Not applicable - the whole premise is multi-month convexity.
family: Calendar and diagonal spreads (time spreads): same-strike calendars, different-strike diagonals, double/triple calendars, double diagonals, PMCC and its put mirror, LEAPS diagonals, calendarized straddles/butterflies, ratio time spreads, and the reverse (short) time spreads
